title: Crisp Parmesan Cream Crackers
summary: Thin, crisp squares of buttery cracker dough rich with grated hard cheese and bound with cream, baked until evenly golden.

ingredients.item: plain flour, plus extra for rolling
fine sea salt or table salt
double cream, plus 1-3 tsp more as needed

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan) and line a tray with baking paper. A fully hot oven sets the thin dough quickly, so the crackers crisp rather than dry out slowly.

steps.title: Crumb
steps.text: Pulse the flour, salt, cheese and cold butter in a food processor until the mixture looks like fine breadcrumbs. Coating the flour in fat now keeps the crackers tender and short.

steps.title: Bind
steps.text: With the motor running, pour in the cream, then add more a teaspoon at a time just until the dough clumps into a ball. It should feel firm, not sticky; too much liquid makes the crackers tough.

steps.title: Roll
steps.text: Roll the dough to 2-3 mm thick on a lightly floured sheet of baking paper. Trim the edges, cut into 5 cm squares without pulling them apart, prick each square twice with a fork and slide the paper onto the tray. Pricking lets steam escape so the crackers stay flat.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake for 10-14 minutes, until evenly golden. The edge pieces colour first, so lift them off early if they are ready before the middle.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Move the crackers to a wire rack and let them cool, then snap them apart along the cuts. They are slightly soft from the oven and crisp up as they cool.

tips: Rolling unevenly is the most common mistake: thick spots stay soft while thin ones burn. Aim for an even 2-3 mm.
Keep the butter cold so the dough stays easy to handle.
Grate the cheese finely so it blends into the dough.
If the dough is too soft to roll, chill it for 15 minutes.
storage: Store in an airtight tin for up to 5 days. If they soften, re-crisp at 180 °C for 3-4 minutes. Unbaked dough can be frozen, well wrapped, for 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
